The vehicle's Human-Machine Interface (HMI) must inform the driver of the operational status of the coordinated control systems, particularly in adverse conditions where wheel-specific adjustments are critical
In case of a critical failure in the steering angle sensor, the vehicle must default to a conservative wheel-specific traction management mode that prioritizes safety
When Adaptive Cruise Control (ACC) is active, the correlation between the steering angle and each wheel speed must be consistent to maintain the intended path and speed without driver intervention
Lane Keeping Assist (LKA) system should adjust the steering angle in response to deviations detected by wheel speed variations, ensuring the vehicle remains within the detected lane
Lane Centering must dynamically adjust the steering angle in conjunction with individual wheel speeds to maintain the vehicle's centered position within the lane, even during curve negotiation
Lane Departure Warning (LDW) system should factor in the wheel speed discrepancies when initiating steering corrections to alert or avert potential lane departures
During an automated lane change, the system must synchronize the steering angle with the wheel speed of each wheel to execute smooth and safe lane transitioning
Traffic Jam Assist must coordinate steering input with each wheel's speed to facilitate precise low-speed maneuvering and lane-keeping in traffic congestion
Automated Emergency Braking (AEB) should consider sudden changes in steering angle and wheel speed as potential indicators of emergency situations to activate braking
Systems responsible for Pedestrian and Cyclist Detection must use steering angle and wheel speed data to adjust the vehicle's trajectory and speed during potential collision scenarios
Blind-spot monitoring (BSM) should use variations in steering angle and wheel speed to calculate the relative motion of adjacent vehicles and alert the driver accordingly
Cross-Traffic Alert (CTA) functionality must be sensitive to the current steering angle and wheel speed to accurately assess the risk of crossing traffic when the vehicle is in motion
The Collision Avoidance System must integrate real-time data from steering angle and wheel speed sensors to orchestrate avoidance maneuvers
Intersection Assist must use steering angle and wheel speed data to make intersection navigation decisions, considering the turning radius and the speed required to execute safe turns
Parking Assistance systems should rely on precise steering angle inputs and controlled wheel speed to automate parking maneuvers accurately
Automated Driving systems, including semi-autonomous and autonomous driving functionalities, must continuously adapt to feedback from the steering angle and wheel speed to navigate safely
